audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer row and every content win[] row reads Warwick or Skill, while the packet chart is Vayne on rows 0-3, Skill on row 4, Vayne on 5-6 — and the whys[] on the same page all say the opposite ("Level 1 favors you", "Level 2 stays yours", "Levels 4-5 remain yours").
audit.why: The chart and its own explanations rendered opposite answers on six of seven rows, at a 51.57% win rate over 989 games.
audit.corrected: All seven rows aligned to the packet chart in both layers, ratings moved with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: The stage explanations were boilerplate and named no spike; phases[5].why claimed the item spike without saying what it beats.
audit.why: Eternal Hunger heals him below 50% health and triples the healing below 25%, so the first-item spike is only real alongside Grievous Wounds; Infinite Duress at 110s is the level-6 spike.
audit.corrected: phases[0..6].why rewritten with the ranges, cooldowns and health thresholds that define each stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl (E) never appears anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: It gives him 2.5s of damage reduction and then fears nearby enemies for 1 second on a 15s cooldown — it blanks your burst window and then breaks your kite, which is exactly the interaction that decides a mid-lane trade.
audit.corrected: Added to dontsFull[1].d and to mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[0].d carried no numbers and dosFull[2].d was a duplicated trading line under a Condemn heading.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is a 1.5s suppress on 110/90/70s; Jaws of the Beast is a 365-range lunge on 8s; Condemn only stuns on terrain collision.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten with cooldowns, the terrain condition and the 25% health threshold.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling early is already in report[8].t, matching the needs-antiheal finding across P, Q and R.

edits.before: Kite with autos and never let him touch you. Identify how Warwick contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Warwick has no gap-closer until Jaws of the Beast is ranked — walk him down with autos and take the level-1 trade.

edits.before: Q tumble resets make your spacing untouchable. Only take the trade when Warwick's Infinite Duress is down.
edits.after: Tumble resets keep you outside his 365-range lunge — trade whenever Jaws of the Beast sits on its 8s.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Warwick must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Condemn is online: Jaws of the Beast is a 365 lunge with no escape, so knock him back and he eats the whole trade.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Infinite Duress's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Still yours: Blood Hunt only speeds him toward targets below 50% health, so stay topped up and he can never close the gap at all.

edits.before: Final Hour stealth-tumbles break every engage pattern onto you. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Warwick's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Infinite Duress suppresses for 1.5s and is up every 110s at rank 1 — hold Condemn for it and the level is a coin-flip at worst.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Infinite Duress's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King plus Grievous Wounds beats the passive heal that triples below 25% health.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Warwick carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on and Final Hour's Tumble invisibility answers his one engage — take every side-lane fight while his R is down.

edits.before: Through 3-5 you keep control by dodging his single gap-closer and kiting; his heal-through-trades is real but you out-space it. Level 6 is the one skill test — respect Infinite Duress, hold E, and the suppress is his only path to a kill.
edits.after: Through 3-5 you keep control by dodging his 365 lunge; Primal Howl cuts his damage taken for 2.5s and then fears you, so break off rather than trade into it. Level 6 is the one skill test — hold Condemn, and the suppress is his only path to a kill.

edits.before: His all-in lock. You can’t kite it. Respect it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a 1.5s suppress on a 110s cooldown at rank 1 — engage after it.

edits.before: Warwick wastes Infinite Duress — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Condemn stuns only into terrain — line his lunge up with the wall first.

edits.before: That is Warwick's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Below 25% health his passive heal triples and Blood Hunt frenzies — never sit there.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Primal Howl cuts damage for 2.5s then fears you — wait it out.

notes: packet suspectName 'Land Infinite Duress' in wants.foe[2] is a FALSE POSITIVE — Infinite Duress is Warwick's real R; left unchanged. This matchup had the worst layer split of the slice: full-layer sides said Warwick on five rows while the content whys on the same page said Vayne. Infinite Duress is flagged 'channel' in the kit, but whether Vayne's Condemn can interrupt the suppress once it has connected is not stated in Riot's text, so no interrupt claim was written.
